mainEntity.name: What does a growth adviser actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: A growth adviser provides forward-looking financial oversight — typically monthly reporting, cash-flow forecasting, budgeting, KPI tracking, and strategic decision support. You get board-level financial insight without a full-time salary. Our matched advisers offer advisory packages scaled to your business size.

mainEntity.name: How is a growth adviser different from my accountant?

acceptedAnswer.text: A compliance accountant looks backward (filing last year's return); a growth adviser looks forward (improving this year's performance). Many firms offer both, and some businesses use the same firm for compliance and advisory. In the questionnaire, tell us whether you want forward-looking growth advice specifically and we will match accordingly.

mainEntity.name: How much does a growth adviser cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Growth advisory typically ranges from $500 to $3,000+ per month depending on engagement depth. Project work (valuation, forecast build, acquisition model) is usually quoted as a fixed fee. The matched adviser will give you a clear quote — the matching itself is free.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will a matched growth adviser contact me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched adviser will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your growth plans.

mainEntity.name: Can a growth adviser help with pricing and margin analysis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser analyses your pricing, identifies margin leaks, and models pricing scenarios — so you can confidently adjust prices to improve profitability without losing customers.

mainEntity.name: Can a growth adviser help with acquisition due diligence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser supports acquisition decisions — financial due diligence, deal structuring, integration planning, and post-acquisition reporting — so you buy with confidence and integrate smoothly.

Yes. The matching service is free for businesses. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched adviser, and the matched firm gives you a clear quote before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: Can a growth adviser build a three-way forecast?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser builds a three-way forecast integrating your profit & loss, balance sheet and cash flow — so you can model growth scenarios and present defensible projections to lenders, boards and investors.

blocks.heading: Business Growth Adviser — what we can help with
blocks.text: SPECIALIST NETWORKBusiness Growth Adviser — what we can help withBeyond the tax returnA growth adviser is the accountant who asks 'how can we improve the business?' rather than 'have you got your receipts?'. They model pricing scenarios, identify margin leaks, forecast cash flow under growth stress, and help you decide whether to hire, acquire, or hold. This is the difference between a compliance accountant and a growth partner — and the right one depends on where your business is.Forward-looking advisory servicesA growth adviser gives you board-level financial oversight without a full-time salary. Typical services include monthly management reporting, cash-flow forecasting, budgeting vs actuals analysis, KPI dashboards, board-pack preparation, and strategic decision support. Our matched growth advisers offer advisory packages tailored to your scale — whether you are a $1m or $20m business.When you need a growth adviserConsider a growth adviser when revenue is growing faster than your confidence about what to do next, when cash flow is tight despite profit, when you are considering hiring senior staff or acquiring another business, or when you want to exit in 3-5 years and need to build the value story now. Our matching connects you with an adviser experienced in your situation.Pricing, margin analysis & M&A due diligenceMargin analysis draws on cost-volume-profit (CVP) analysis and pricing strategy — core management accounting competencies that identify where margin leaks and help you set prices with confidence. For acquisitions, mid-market accounting practices regularly perform buy-side financial due diligence on a project-fee basis, including Quality of Earnings analysis, balance sheet reviews, and working capital checks. There is an important regulatory boundary to understand: providing financial due diligence or general valuation work on a business target does not require an Australian Financial Services Licence (AFSL). However, where an acquisition involves structuring regulated financial products, advice must be delivered by an appropriately licensed entity under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth). Our matched growth advisers are clear about where their expertise ends and where licensed financial advice is required.
